findings.evidence: Lines 87–94 construct the canonical map as a local `let e`, while lines 95–110 prove only its value at `π`. The parallel API in `ClassFieldTheory/Brauer/Unramified.lean:146–168` publicly defines `unramifiedInvEquiv` and provides the `[simp]` evaluation theorem `unramifiedInvEquiv_unramifiedClass`.
findings.fix: Expose a canonical noncomputable additive equivalence built from `normalizedValuationMod`, with an `@[simp]` lemma sending every `QuotientGroup.mk x` to `normalizedValuationMod ... (Additive.ofMul x)`, and derive this existential uniformizer theorem from it.
findings.issue: `localNormQuotientEquivZMod_unramified` existentially packages the equivalence and characterizes it only on one uniformizer, despite claiming that normalized valuation induces it; consumers cannot name the map or simplify its value on an arbitrary quotient class.

summary: The public result hides the canonical valuation-induced equivalence and exposes only its existence, leaving consumers without an evaluation API.
